answers.question: No tools were defined, so here is the smallest tool set I propose, for you to confirm. (a) Look up orders, in the order system: returns each of the signed-in customer's orders, cancelled ones included, each with its refund or none; it can get no answer. (b) Cancel order (order number), in the order system: answers cancelled, not cancellable with the order's status (shipped or delivered), or order not found, or gets no answer; cancelling an order that is already cancelled answers cancelled. (c) Issue refund (order number), in the order system, which calls the payment provider: refunds the order's total paid to its payment method and answers with the refund, status pending or issued; on a terminal error it answers with a refund whose status is failed; on a transient error it creates none; or it gets no answer. (d) Create staff follow-up (order number, reason), in the staff task queue: reasons are refund not issued, refund status unknown, cancellation unknown, and refund amount differs; it creates the task or gets no answer, and a call with no answer is not retried. Is this the tool set?
answers.reply:
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Your order system has no docs, so I compared it with common payment systems. In those, a second refund call for the same payment creates a second refund (Stripe's docs: "You can issue more than one refund against a charge"). Your rules say an order gets at most one refund, and that after a refund call with no answer the agent retries once. If your order system creates no second refund for an order that already has one, the retry is safe: the agent retries, and the retry answers with the refund the first call made. If it would create a second refund, the agent must look the order up before retrying and retry only when no refund is there. Which holds? Claims put to the owner: C-13.
answers.recommended: The order system creates no second refund: a refund call for an order that already has a refund answers with that refund.
answers.reply: > Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.

answers.question: When the cancel call gets no answer, the order may or may not have been cancelled, as in common order systems. Shortest path: the customer says yes, the cancel call gets no answer, and then the agent either issues the refund (and may refund an order that was never cancelled) or does not. What should the agent do? Claims put to the owner: C-10.
answers.recommended: The agent makes no refund call, hands the case to store staff as "cancellation unknown", and tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled and that store staff will follow up.
answers.reply: > Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.

answers.question: The agent tells the customer the refund amount the refund call returns. What does the agent do when that amount differs from the amount the customer said yes to?
answers.recommended: The agent makes no further change with the new amount, tells the customer the amount the refund call returned, and hands the case to store staff (reason: refund amount differs).
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.
